title: Quantum Optimization, Semidefinite Programs, and Variational Algorithms

items.title: Trace of a product of Hermitian matrices is real
items.statement: For finite-dimensional Hermitian matrices A and B of the same size, Tr(AB) is real.

references.title: Joran van Apeldoorn et al., Quantum SDP-solvers: Better upper and lower bounds

proof_obligations: Use an orthonormal basis, the conjugate-transpose matrix of an adjoint, adjoint product reversal, and rectangular trace cyclicity.

items.title: Trace of a product of positive semidefinite matrices is nonnegative
items.statement: For finite-dimensional positive semidefinite matrices P and Q of the same size, Tr(PQ) is a nonnegative real number.

references.title: Joran van Apeldoorn et al., Quantum SDP-solvers: Better upper and lower bounds

proof_obligations: Use the nonnegative square root, cyclicity, and the quadratic-form definition; include dimension zero.

items.title: Finite semidefinite primal-dual pair
items.statement: For Hermitian C,A_1,…,A_m∈C^{n×n} and b∈R^m, the primal SDP maximizes Tr(CX) over X⪰0 subject to Tr(A_jX)≤b_j. Its dual minimizes b·y over y∈R^m with y≥0 and Σ_j y_jA_j−C⪰0. Feasibility, attainment, trace bounds and all normalization assumptions are separate promises, not consequences of the definition.
proof_obligations: Check real-valuedness of traces of products of Hermitian matrices in these constraints.
Distinguish primal and dual variables and signs; state dimensions and finite-dimensional positivity convention.

items.title: Normalized Hermitian observable defines a two-outcome POVM
items.statement: For finite Hermitian M with ||M||≤1, E_+=(I+M)/2 and E_-=(I−M)/2 are positive effects summing to I. On a density matrix ρ, assigning output +1 to E_+ and −1 to E_- has mean Tr(Mρ).
proof_obligations: Diagonalize M and use each eigenvalue in [−1,1] to prove 0≤E_±≤I and E_++E_−=I.
Use trace linearity and Tr(ρ)=1 to compute Tr(E_+ρ)−Tr(E_-ρ)=Tr(Mρ), with the declared Dirac/trace convention.

items.title: Matrix multiplicative-weights game and update
items.statement: For dimension n and rounds t=1,…,T, an adversary supplies Hermitian loss matrices M_t with −I⪯M_t⪯I. Given η∈(0,1], define W_t=exp(−ηΣ_{s<t}M_s) and the density matrix ρ_t=W_t/Tr(W_t). The cost at round t is Tr(M_tρ_t). All exponentials are finite-dimensional matrix exponentials defined by the Hermitian spectral functional calculus.
proof_obligations: Prove W_t is positive definite and Tr(W_t)>0 by the spectral theorem.
Derive ρ_t⪰0 and Tr(ρ_t)=1.
Distinguish update indexing and sign conventions from the cited MMW presentation.

items.title: Weak duality for the finite SDP pair
items.statement: For every primal-feasible X and dual-feasible y, Tr(CX)≤b·y. In fact b·y−Tr(CX)=Σ_j y_j(b_j−Tr(A_jX))+Tr((Σ_jy_jA_j−C)X), and each summand is nonnegative.
proof_obligations: Show the scalar constraint terms are nonnegative because y_j≥0.
For positive semidefinite P,Q, write Tr(PQ)=Tr(P^{1/2}QP^{1/2})≥0 using cyclicity and the nonnegative square-root theorem.
Conclude weak duality without assuming strong duality or optimizer attainment.

items.title: Scalar exponential bound for bounded losses
items.statement: For 0<η≤1 and every real x∈[−1,1], e^{−ηx}≤1−ηx+η². Therefore for Hermitian −I⪯M⪯I, e^{−ηM}⪯I−ηM+η²I in the Loewner order.
proof_obligations: Use the scalar Taylor series with a remainder bound on |ηx|≤1, then apply the Hermitian spectral theorem eigenvalue by eigenvalue.
State the chosen constant and verify it controls both signs of x.

items.title: Matrix multiplicative-weights regret bound
items.statement: For every sequence −I⪯M_t⪯I and η∈(0,1], the update above satisfies Σ_{t=1}^T Tr(M_tρ_t)≤λ_min(Σ_{t=1}^T M_t)+ηT+(log n)/η, with logarithm and constants translated to the selected base convention.
proof_obligations: Define the partition function Z_t=Tr exp(−ηΣ_{s≤t}M_s); bound successive ratios using Golden–Thompson and the scalar exponential estimate.
Lower-bound Z_{T+1} by exp(−ηλ_min(ΣM_t)) and upper-bound the initial potential by n.
Combine logarithms and divide by η, checking whether the stated η² constant changes the additive ηT term.

items.title: No-failure MMW rounds yield an approximate dual-feasible vector
items.statement: In the normalized SDP with A₁=I, b₁=R>0, ||A_j||,||C||≤1 and an attained optimal dual vector of ℓ₁ norm at most r≥1, let w=r+1 and M_t=(Σ_j y_{t,j}A_j−C)/w. Suppose each round has y_t≥0, ||y_t||₁≤r, b·y_t≤α, trace estimates ã_t,j,c̃_t within θ of Tr(A_jρ_t),Tr(Cρ_t), and Σ_j y_t,j ã_t,j−c̃_t≥−wθ. If γ≥w(2θ+η+ln(n)/(ηT)), then ȳ=γe₁+T⁻¹Σ_t y_t is dual feasible and b·ȳ≤α+γR.

references.title: Joran van Apeldoorn et al., Quantum SDP-solvers: Better upper and lower bounds

proof_obligations: Derive the actual loss lower bound from the finite trace errors, apply the local MMW regret bound, shift by A₁=I, and track the objective increment.

items.title: Parameterized variational quantum objective
items.statement: A finite VQA consists of parameter domain Θ⊆R^p, supplied parameterized circuit U(θ), finite input states ρ_k, observables O_k, and objective C(θ)=Σ_k f_k(Tr[O_k U(θ)ρ_k U(θ)†]). Specify how each input state is prepared and charged, whether the algorithm minimizes or maximizes C, how estimates are obtained from measurements, the classical optimizer and stopping rule, and the output object. No existence, convergence, global optimality, or advantage follows from this definition.
proof_obligations: Show each trace is real when O_k is Hermitian and the output state is positive with unit trace.
State the finite shot/noise and parameter precision model and charge each circuit evaluation.
Do not silently assume that the classical optimizer finds a global minimizer.
Charge preparation of every ρ_k and the parameterized ansatz circuit at each classical objective/gradient query.

items.title: Classical optimizer interface for hybrid algorithms
items.statement: A hybrid optimizer is an explicitly specified classical procedure receiving finite-precision estimates of C(θ) or its derivatives and returning parameter queries and a stopping/output rule. Any guarantee must list assumptions such as convexity, smoothness, domain geometry, noise bounds, and initialization; the VQA definition alone carries no convergence rate.
proof_obligations: State the exact oracle precision and number of calls for a claimed optimizer theorem.
Check the objective assumptions against the actual parameterized circuit; do not assume a nonconvex VQA landscape is convex.

items.title: QAOA circuit and expected combinatorial objective
items.statement: For a finite graph G=(V,E), define the MaxCut cost operator C_G=Σ_{(u,v)∈E}(I−Z_uZ_v)/2 and mixer B=Σ_{v∈V}X_v. At depth p and angles (γ_1,…,γ_p,β_1,…,β_p), prepare |+⟩^{⊗|V|}, apply ∏_{j=p}^{1} e^{−iβ_j B}e^{−iγ_j C_G} in declared order, and score the expected cut value ⟨ψ(γ,β)|C_G|ψ(γ,β)⟩. Measurement outputs a random cut under the circuit distribution.

references.title: Edward Farhi, Jeffrey Goldstone, and Sam Gutmann, A Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (arXiv:1411.4028v1)

proof_obligations: Check each edge term is the 0/1 indicator of a cut in the computational basis.
Derive the expectation as an average cut score and distinguish it from the maximum cut value.
State gate implementation, graph loading, parameter precision and measurement cost.

items.title: Variational eigenvalue objective
items.statement: For finite Hermitian H and normalized ansatz state |ψ(θ)⟩=U(θ)|ψ_0⟩, the VQE objective is E(θ)=⟨ψ(θ)|H|ψ(θ)⟩_D. The target ground energy is E_0=min σ(H); the ansatz is variational because every feasible state has energy at least E_0.
proof_obligations: Translate Dirac expectation to the root linear-first convention and expand the state in an orthonormal eigenbasis.

items.title: Parameter-shift derivative for a Pauli generator
items.statement: If a parameter appears in one gate U_j(θ)=e^{−iθP/2} with Hermitian P satisfying P²=I, and all other circuit factors and the observable are independent of θ, then ∂_θ C(θ)=½(C(θ+π/2)−C(θ−π/2)) for each linear expectation term. The identity is exact; estimating the two shifted costs from finite shots adds sampling error and measurement cost.
proof_obligations: Write each expectation as a finite trigonometric polynomial of θ with frequencies at most one because the generator eigenvalues are ±1/2.
Differentiate that expression and verify the shifted difference equals the derivative.
For sums/compositions, apply linearity/chain rule only under the stated cost form; do not generalize to arbitrary generators without a new spectral-gap formula.

items.title: QAOA objective is an expected feasible score only
items.statement: The QAOA expectation lies between the minimum and maximum feasible cut values, and each measured bitstring is a feasible cut. An expected value guarantee alone does not imply a universal approximation ratio or global optimality; such a theorem requires additional graph/depth/optimizer hypotheses.

references.title: Edward Farhi, Jeffrey Goldstone, and Sam Gutmann, A Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (arXiv:1411.4028v1)

proof_obligations: Expand the expectation over the finite measurement distribution and use the pointwise cut-score bounds.
Give or cite no unsupported universal convergence, approximation-ratio, or quantum-advantage claim.

items.title: VQE Rayleigh–Ritz upper bound and equality case
items.statement: For every θ, E(θ)≥E_0, with equality exactly when |ψ(θ)⟩ lies in the ground eigenspace. Therefore an optimizer restricted to an ansatz family can certify an upper bound on E_0, but no guarantee that it reaches E_0 follows unless the family contains a ground state and the classical optimization actually finds it.
proof_obligations: Expand in an orthonormal eigenbasis and express E(θ)−E_0 as Σ_j(λ_j−E_0)|c_j|².
Characterize equality by support only on the minimum-eigenvalue eigenspace; allow degeneracy.

items.title: Capped randomized amplitude amplification preserves a flagged output
items.statement: Let V be a supplied finite-dimensional unitary preparation, Π a supplied success projector, and |0⟩ the declared initial vector. Let p=||ΠV|0>||²≥p_low>0, where p_low is a supplied positive rational, and let 0<ρ<1 be a supplied rational failure target. The finite capped procedure returns the normalized good projection ΠV|0>/√p (up to global phase) with probability at least 1−ρ. If p_low≥1/2 it uses direct verified samples. Otherwise each round first takes one direct sample; after failure it draws b=ceil(log₂K) fair bits, K=ceil(1/sqrt(p_low)), obtaining J uniformly from 0,…,2^b−1, and runs J Grover iterations only when J<K. J≥K counts as that round’s randomized-branch failure. Use N=ceil(16 ln(1/ρ))+16 fresh rounds. Its calls to V,V†, reflections, verifier, bN random bits and output are explicit; the call count is O(p_low^(-1/2)(1+ln(1/ρ))).

references.title: Brassard, Høyer, Mosca, and Tapp, Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms

proof_obligations: Prove the two-dimensional good/bad rotation, the uniform integer-iteration mean bound, conditional output-state preservation, and finite-round failure bound.

items.title: SDP maximally entangled reference-state access
items.statement: For matrix dimension d, define |Φ_d⟩=d^(−1/2)Σ_{i=0}^{d−1}|i⟩|i⟩. The access model supplies a preparation circuit V_Φ and inverse with costs C_Φ, width and ancillas. If d=2^q, apply H to each of q first-register qubits and then a CNOT from each first-register qubit to the matching second-register qubit; this uses exactly q Hadamards and q CNOTs on 2q wires. For arbitrary d, V_Φ and its cost are supplied inputs unless a separate explicit construction is proved.
proof_obligations: Derive the uniform superposition after H^⊗q and verify that the CNOT layer copies each basis label, giving d^(-1/2)Σ_i|i,i⟩.
For non-power-of-two d, specify an exact preparation procedure, output support and cost; do not pad the Gibbs operator in a way that changes its trace without accounting for the added eigenvalues.
Charge V_Φ,V_Φ†, input encoding, any finite gate synthesis, and width/ancilla costs.
unresolved_obligations: No general efficient circuit for arbitrary non-power-of-two d is claimed; retain C_Φ unless a separate construction and cost proof is supplied.

items.title: Flagged trace ratio returns a Gibbs-state observable mean
items.statement: For Hermitian G and M with ||M||≤1, let g=exp(−G/2), B>0, and |Φ_d>=d^(−1/2)Σ_i|i,i>. If p_M is the all-zero-work probability after applying g(G)/B and then the block with squared compression (I+M/2)/4 to the first half, and p_0 is the same probability with M=0, then p_M/p_0=1+(1/2)Tr(Mρ_G), where ρ_G=exp(−G)/Tr(exp(−G)); in particular p_0>0.

references.title: Joran van Apeldoorn et al., Quantum SDP-solvers: Better upper and lower bounds

proof_obligations: Compute both finite success probabilities from the maximally entangled vectorization identity and use trace cyclicity.

items.title: Quantum convex membership and weak-separation model
items.statement: Let K⊂R^n be closed convex with Euclidean balls B(0,r)⊆K⊆B(0,R). Define a weak membership oracle MEM_{ε,0}(K) with its promised inner/outer boundary behavior and a weak separation oracle SEP_{η,ρ}(K) that, on a point outside the shrunken set, returns a separating hyperplane with failure at most ρ. Precision, inverse coherent access and output bit costs are explicit.
proof_obligations: State the membership/separation boundary conventions and the exact domain on which correctness is promised.
Check the radius and error parameters have compatible units and include the oracle’s classical output encoding.

items.title: Sparse SDP matrix access and computational model
items.statement: For C,A_1,…,A_m, specify sparsity s and reversible oracles O_I that return the column of the ℓth nonzero entry of row k (including padded sentinel behavior) and O_M that XOR-returns a finite-precision entry. Specify whether inverse access is supplied. Record matrix-entry bit precision, classical preprocessing, and any access to sparse sums H(t)=Σ_j y_jA_j separately. If QRAM is invoked, state its exact unitary action, construction, gate/time cost and whether a source theorem counts it at unit cost; no QRAM operation is assigned cost zero by this definition.
proof_obligations: Prove all index/value maps reversible on every input basis state and specify exact arithmetic/rounding.
Separate matrix-entry queries, sparse-sum access, QRAM, quantum gates, classical control, and state preparation.
Do not identify oracle complexity with a standard gate complexity without implementing the oracle.

items.title: Quantum membership-to-separation procedure
items.statement: For a convex body K with B(0,r)⊆K⊆B(0,R), run the van Apeldoorn et al. quantum gradient-based weak-separation construction using coherent membership-oracle access and its inverse. Given η∈(0,R], ρ∈(0,1/3], and membership precision ε bounded as in Theorem 23, it returns the promised weak separating hyperplane with failure at most ρ. The complete binding generation/execution definition is operational-contracts.md OP7, including OP0 numerical/selection subroutines, every cap/failure/invalid branch, access direction, output and cost convention. Its instructions are part of this Definition; named source routines are expanded there rather than assumed available.
proof_obligations: Reproduce the smoothing/gradient construction and its boundary margin from the full Theorem 23 proof.
Track membership precision ε≤η(58n)^{−9/2}(r/R)^3(η/R)^2ρ and every oracle/inverse query.
State the exact output precision and any classical arithmetic used.
unresolved_obligations: The weak-separation theorem has a complete source proof but must be authored as local proof obligations; only the stated ball and oracle promises support it.

The binding appendix defines the finite procedure now; prove its explicit precision constants, capped-schedule correctness/termination and actual query/gate/bit resource bounds locally. Source guarantees are not automatically accepted for modified schedules or coefficient profiles.

items.title: Quantum weak-separation query bound
items.statement: Under the preceding radius, precision and failure assumptions, Theorem 23 gives O(log(n/ρ)·log((n/ρ)(R/η)(R/r))) quantum queries to MEM_{ε,0}(K) and its inverse to implement SEP_{η,ρ}(K). Composing with the cited classical optimization-from-separation reduction yields Õ(n) membership queries under its own interior-radius and weak-oracle hypotheses; output/gate/bit costs are additional.
proof_obligations: Transcribe the full Theorem 23 expression and parameter restrictions; prove the composition cost from the classical separation-to-optimization routine.
Do not assert the Õ(n) optimization corollary without its weak-oracle, precision, radius and classical-optimization assumptions.
unresolved_obligations: The classical separation-to-optimization reduction is not an existing root supplier; its exact finite-dimensional proof or an explicit named supplier is required before the corollary is promoted.

items.title: Sparse-oracle Gibbs-state purification
items.statement: Given a finite Hermitian loss matrix H with a declared spectral interval and sparse-entry/sparse-sum access, approximate the scalar function g(x)=exp(−ηx/2) on that interval by an explicit bounded polynomial, prepare |Φ_d⟩ using the access contract (exactly q Hadamards and q CNOTs for d=2^q; otherwise use supplied V_Φ with cost C_Φ) and apply the matrix-function circuit to one half, and postselect/amplify the success flag. The normalized output is a purification of ρ_H=exp(−ηH)/Tr(exp(−ηH)); the polynomial, approximation error, success probability and all access costs are explicit inputs. Executable input includes certified polynomial approximations and their phase lists. For non-parity g, split g into even and odd components on a symmetric interval, block-encode both divided by a common β≥sup|g|, and use costed two-term LCU to encode g/(2β); then ideal success probability is Tr(exp(−ηH))/(4β²d). Charge β, complement/phase generation, LCU and postselection separately. A bare scalar-function existence statement does not generate those circuits. The complete binding generation/execution definition is operational-contracts.md OP8, including OP0 numerical/selection subroutines, every cap/failure/invalid branch, access direction, output and cost convention. Its instructions are part of this Definition; named source routines are expanded there rather than assumed available.
proof_obligations: Prove the scalar polynomial is bounded and uniformly approximates g over the entire promised spectrum.
Use the spectral theorem to calculate the reduced density matrix and normalize the purification.
Lower-bound the success probability from the interval/norm assumptions and charge state preparation, block encoding, QSVT, amplification and inverse calls.

Give the finite amplitude-table encoding and preparation cost for the maximally entangled reference state; if QC24 synthesizes it, state D, width, rotation/gate counts, table storage and finite-precision costs.
Use the explicit H/CNOT construction for power-of-two matrix dimension; for other dimensions carry C_Φ as an input parameter and do not infer it from the QC24 amplitude-table bound.
unresolved_obligations: The algorithm is a proposed finite-matrix reconstruction of the source’s Gibbs-state step; no matrix exponential or Gibbs preparation circuit is free.
For arbitrary dimension d, the supplied reference-state cost C_Φ must be charged; source gate scaling is retained only if C_Φ and all other explicit costs fit the stated bound.

The binding appendix defines the finite procedure now; prove its explicit precision constants, capped-schedule correctness/termination and actual query/gate/bit resource bounds locally. Source guarantees are not automatically accepted for modified schedules or coefficient profiles.

items.title: Gibbs purification error and resource bound
items.statement: If the unnormalized ideal Gibbs amplitude has success probability p_G>0 and the implemented flagged amplitude differs by at most ζ with ζ≤√p_G/2, then the normalized conditional purification differs in vector norm by at most 2ζ/√p_G, actual success is at least p_G/4, and capped amplification succeeds with probability at least 2/3 at cost O(p_G^(-1/2)) preparation/reflection calls plus the explicit block, state-preparation, and compilation costs.
proof_obligations: Apply the QSVT operator error theorem, bound the unnormalized vector error on the maximally entangled input, and prove the normalized-state perturbation inequality.
Include all simulation, phase compilation, success amplification and state-preparation errors in ζ; provide a lower bound for p_G.
unresolved_obligations: The paper-specific degree, spectral interval, success lower bound, and error allocation must be instantiated before this conditional theorem yields the source complexity.

items.title: Coherent SDP matrix-expectation oracle
items.statement: Given a purification of a density matrix ρ and Hermitian observable M with ||M||≤1 and block/measurement access to (I+M)/2, use a coherent ±1-valued measurement sampler whose mean is Tr(Mρ), then invoke the QA29 expectation estimator. Supply preparation of the purification and its inverse, observable access, good reflection, controlled calls and finite-precision encoding. The complete binding generation/execution definition is operational-contracts.md OP8, including OP0 numerical/selection subroutines, every cap/failure/invalid branch, access direction, output and cost convention. Its instructions are part of this Definition; named source routines are expanded there rather than assumed available.
proof_obligations: Derive the two-outcome probabilities from the purification’s reduced state and the POVM effects (I±M)/2.
Show the encoded random variable has mean Tr(Mρ) and lies in [−1,1].
Use QA29 without duplicating amplitude estimation and charge each purification/measurement access.
unresolved_obligations: The final QC measurement/instrument semantics and observable-access implementation must be reconciled; a classical matrix does not provide an observable oracle.

The binding appendix defines the finite procedure now; prove its explicit precision constants, capped-schedule correctness/termination and actual query/gate/bit resource bounds locally. Source guarantees are not automatically accepted for modified schedules or coefficient profiles.

items.title: SDP matrix-expectation estimation error and cost
items.statement: For ||M||≤1, the QA29 amplitude-estimation sampler estimates Tr(Mρ) within additive τ and failure δ using O(τ^{-1}log(1/δ)) coherent expectation-oracle rounds; total cost multiplies by the stated Gibbs-purification, observable and inverse-oracle costs and includes preparation error. In the SDP iteration, select τ and δ so all m estimates and the Gibbs-state perturbation remain within the source’s per-round tolerance.
proof_obligations: Apply QA29 after the ±1 encoding, use a union bound across m observables, and combine measurement and purification errors.
Substitute the per-iteration tolerance into the total rounds and include all state/oracle costs.
unresolved_obligations: The theorem gives an access-parameterized estimator; the advertised SDP query exponent requires the source’s concrete oracle realization and precision schedule.

items.title: Matrix-weights regret implies SDP approximate feasibility
items.statement: For the source’s primal-dual feasibility game, if each round’s matrix expectations are known within τ and the MMW regret is at most ηT+log(n)/η, then the averaged queried dual weights produce a feasible dual candidate up to the declared τ/η slack; if the feasibility oracle rejects, the accumulated primal density matrices yield a primal candidate meeting the complementary objective threshold. The exact source normalization and width parameter w=r+1 are part of the statement.
proof_obligations: Write the source’s loss matrix, width bound and primal/dual accumulated variables explicitly.
Insert the MMW regret inequality, control the expectation-estimation perturbation by Tτ, and derive each constraint and objective slack.
Use weak duality to rule out simultaneous strict primal and dual certificates.

items.title: Binary search converts feasibility to additive SDP optimization
items.statement: Assume the source feasibility oracle distinguishes objective thresholds α with total slack at most ε/4, the optimum lies in [−R,R], and all oracle failures are budgeted to total probability at most 1/3. A binary-search procedure with O(log(R/ε)) threshold queries returns a feasible dual vector with objective at most OPT+ε (and uses the source’s feasible-certificate rule when a threshold is rejected).
proof_obligations: Prove the binary-search interval invariant, finite termination, accumulated feasibility/threshold error, and returned-certificate objective bound.
Allocate failure probabilities across all calls and include the logarithmic threshold count in the tilde notation.

items.title: Sparse-oracle quantum SDP algorithm
items.statement: On the full normalized sparse-SDP promises of QA30, run the finite OP8 coefficient, spectral-minimum, Gibbs/flagged-trace, sparse-sum, two-sparse-oracle, MMW threshold and slack-aware binary-search procedures. Return a stored sparse dual list only after its certificate checks; statistical, capped, arithmetic, or interval uncertainty returns an explicit UNDECIDED/FAIL branch, never HIGHER. The separately defined normalized Gibbs-purification and supplied-normalized-purification measurement interfaces remain included. Costs distinguish matrix queries, sparse-sum access, QRAM construction/updates, gates, coefficients, bits, and state preparation.
proof_obligations: Specify the source’s primal and dual feasibility conditions, norm bounds, A_1=I,b_1=R, primal trace bound R, attained dual optimum and ℓ1 bound r≥1.
Prove the MMW-to-SDP feasibility reduction, binary-search invariant, error allocations, Gibbs-state approximation and trace-estimation correctness.
Construct each sparse-sum index/value oracle and include its QRAM/data-structure construction cost; no state preparation or sparse-sum oracle is free.
Keep the output as a classical dual vector and state its bit-precision and measurement/repetition cost.
unresolved_obligations: An end-to-end theorem needs the complete local Arora–Kale reduction, matrix-function/Gibbs preparation, estimation and sparse-sum oracle proofs plus review of the Golden–Thompson draft. The Õ query bound is not a standard-circuit gate bound until QRAM is implemented and charged.

The binding appendix defines the finite procedure now; prove its explicit precision constants, capped-schedule correctness/termination and actual query/gate/bit resource bounds locally. Source guarantees are not automatically accepted for modified schedules or coefficient profiles.

items.title: Quantum SDP additive-optimality guarantee
items.statement: For the paper’s normalized sparse SDP with ||A_j||,||C||≤1, A_1=I, b_1=R, primal optimal trace at most R, attained dual optimum with an optimal dual vector of ℓ_1 norm at most r≥1, and maximum matrix sparsity s, the solver returns with probability at least 2/3 a feasible dual vector y whose objective is within additive ε of the optimum. The guarantee is for the stated sparse input and sparse-sum oracle model; it does not output a dense primal matrix or a classical optimizer for arbitrary objectives.
proof_obligations: Use the source’s exact feasibility and dual-attainment assumptions; derive strong optimal comparison only where the theorem’s assumptions give primal/dual attainment.
Track all MMW, Gibbs-state, trace-estimation, binary-search and failure errors so their sum is ≤ε.
Use weak duality for the feasible output and the source’s feasibility argument for ε-optimality.
unresolved_obligations: The statement is not ready for publication until the full source proof is authored and the draft Golden–Thompson supplier is reviewed; the 2/3 success is a weakened consequence of “high probability.”

items.title: Quantum SDP query bound and QRAM cost boundary
items.statement: The source reports Õ(√(nm)s²(Rr/ε)^8) queries to input matrix oracles and the same order of quantum gates in its stated computational model; for diagonal LPs it reports exponent 5. The general theorem uses a unit-cost QRAM primitive in the sparse-sum access implementation in Appendix D. QA5’s decomposed circuit cost additionally includes each reference-state preparation C_Φ, Gibbs/QSVT preparation, matrix-expectation access, QRAM/data-structure operations, and state preparation; the source gate bound applies to this implementation only when these explicit costs fit within that tilde bound. Otherwise report the query theorem and add the actual preparation/access costs rather than claiming the source gate bound.
proof_obligations: Trace every sparse-sum access through the algorithm and count its input-oracle calls, QRAM operations, quantum gates and classical operations separately.
Track each reference-state and Gibbs-state preparation; compare its explicit cost to the source theorem’s gate bound, or add the full cost as a separate term.
Preserve tilde-log factors and the exact R,r,s,ε dependence; do not suppress input/output costs.
Verify the LP exponent-5 restriction and do not generalize it to arbitrary SDPs.
unresolved_obligations: The arbitrary-dimension reference-state preparation cost C_Φ must be shown to fit the advertised gate bound, or carried as an additive cost parameter; the generic QC24 table upper bound alone does not establish this.

title: Quantum Optimization, Semidefinite Programs, and Variational Algorithms — Examples

items.title: A one-constraint scalar SDP and its dual
items.statement: Solve a one-dimensional SDP explicitly and verify weak duality and an attained optimum under stated feasibility assumptions.
proof_obligations: Check primal/dual signs, feasible sets, objective values, and distinguish weak from strong duality.

items.title: A variational circuit family may miss the optimum
items.statement: Choose a finite Hermitian matrix with ground state orthogonal to the states in a restricted ansatz family. The variational bound remains valid, but no parameter in that family attains the ground energy.
proof_obligations: Compute the ansatz energy range and ground energy and show the strict gap; this refutes a universal global-optimum claim.

items.title: VQE and MaxCut-QAOA objective calculation
items.statement: For a two-qubit Hamiltonian and a one-edge graph, calculate a parameterized VQE energy and QAOA expected cut, including the outcome distribution for the declared parameters.

references.title: Edward Farhi, Jeffrey Goldstone, and Sam Gutmann, A Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (arXiv:1411.4028v1)

proof_obligations: Verify the Rayleigh upper bound and show that a finite-depth objective value is not by itself a universal optimizer guarantee.
